architecture.name: bridge-d256-route-comparison
architecture.head_dims: Comparison target: head_dim 256 attention forward on sm_75 (Turing) against the current bridge-native kernel at d=64/128 (/opt/repo/agentic-vllm/software/vllm/sm75-marlin/turing_lab/bridge/flash_fwd_sm75.cuh: 64x64 tiles, 4 warps, m16n8k8 mma, ldmatrix B-fragments, causal tile skipping, online softmax with h2exp2). Baseline coverage sets: llama.cpp fattn-mma Turing config table covers 256/256, 320/256, 512/512, 576/512 (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-mma-f16.cuh, ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_turing); FA2 templates 32-256; ssiu/flash-attention-turing d=64/128; FlashInfer decode 64/128/256.
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: Primary target is qk_dim = v_dim = 256 (Gemma-2/Gemma-3-style). Divergent shapes (DeepSeek MLA qk 576 / v 512) are not natural targets for ROUTE A (monolithic d=256 template) but are proven feasible on Turing via k-chunking: llama.cpp fattn-mma's Turing table ships 576/512 and 512/512 configs (nbatch_K2 chunking of the D axis), and FFPA (DefTruth, flash-attention #1474/#1483) demonstrates D up to 1024 with O(1) SRAM. ROUTE B (k-chunking) is the only route that extends to qk!=v shapes for free since QK^T and PV chunk independently over the head dim.
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: Bridge kernel v1 has no GQA yet; ROUTE A/B inherit that debt. Same-hardware precedents: llama.cpp fattn-mma handles GQA via ncols per CTA (8/16/32/64) including on the Turing 256/256 config; vLLM PagedAttention V0 kernel has no GQA (added later); FA2/FlashInfer support GQA natively on sm80+ but their sm_75 story is blocked elsewhere (see capability_gate).
architecture.hybrid_pattern: Not a linear-vs-full hybrid question, but the dominant d=256 consumer models shape the workload: Gemma-3 is a 5:1 local (sliding window 1024):global full-attention pattern, so a d=256 sm_75 kernel spends much of its time on short effective KV windows, where causal tile skipping (already in flash_fwd_sm75.cuh) and decode (split-KV) efficiency matter more than peak prefill TFLOPS. [uncertain: deployment mix of Gemma-3 on Turing fleets]
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: No mainstream model mixes d=128 and d=256 per layer today (Gemma-2/3 are uniform d=256). The bridge template dispatch (template<int D>) extends to a 3-way {64,128,256} instantiation under ROUTE A/B; under ROUTE C unmodified FA2/FlashInfer would cover all their dims at once, but only on architectures where they actually run (see capability_gate).

kernel_support.supported_dims: ROUTE A: a native d=256 template instantiation of flash_fwd_sm75.cuh requires 32-row KV tiles (K/V smem 2x32x264x2B = 33.8KB) plus a Q-in-registers redesign (drop qf[D/8][2]; at d=256 Q fragments alone are 64 registers). With 64-row KV tiles smem = 3x64x264x2 = 101,376B > 64KB, impossible on Turing; with 32-row KV tiles and the +8 pad kept it is 67,584B, still 2KB over the 65,536B cap - so pad must be dropped (64+32+32 rows x 256 x 2B = exactly 65,536B) or the Q tile shrunk to 32 rows (3x32x264x2 = 50.7KB). ROUTE B: keeps the existing 128-deep pipeline, chains two 128-deep mma sequences for S=QK^T accumulation and two for PV; K/V smem stays at today's 51KB (d=128 layout) if each k-half is staged serially into the same buffer (2 extra stage+barrier passes per tile instead of smem doubling). ROUTE C: zero new kernel code - FA2 master already carries sub-sm80 fallback branches (kernel_traits.h: MMA_Atom SM75_16x8x8_F32F16F16F32_TN, SmemCopyAtom SM75_U32x4_LDSM_N / SM75_U16x8_LDSM_T i.e. native ldmatrix, Gmem_copy_struct falls back from SM80_CP_ASYNC_CACHEGLOBAL to AutoVectorizingCopyWithAssumedAlignment<128> register staging, Element forced to half_t), and flash_fwd_kernel.h's PV path calls convert_layout_acc_Aregs with an explicit 'if using m16n8k8' comment - but the launch template gates kernel bodies with ARCH_SUPPORTS_FLASH (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800) and prints 'FATAL: FlashAttention requires building with sm version sm80-sm90' below sm80, so 'unmodified' is in practice 'one-gate-patch plus debugging'.
kernel_support.capability_gate: Real sm_75 blockers: (1) shared memory: 64KB per SM and 64KB per-block opt-in (no Ampere-style 99/163KB) - this is what kills FA2's shipped d=256 fwd configs (A100 dispatch (kBlockM=128,kBlockN=64,8 warps) = 131,072B = 128KB; H100 dispatch (64,64,4) = 98,304B = 96KB; only the commented-out (64,32,4) traits hit exactly 65,536B = 64KB); (2) no cp.async - everything degrades to synchronous LDG->STS with zero overlap (llama.cpp fattn-mma sets nstages=0 on Turing for the same reason; ssiu's Turing port lives with it); (3) bf16 absent - FA2 kernel_traits literally forces Element=half_t below sm80; (4) GeForce-Turing tensor cores run mma f32.f16.f16.f32 at HALF rate vs f16 accumulate (2080 Ti: 54.2 vs 108 TFLOPS per NVIDIA Turing whitepaper; T4: 65 TFLOPS in both modes per the whitepaper table) - relevant because the bridge kernel and FA2/FFPA all use fp32 accumulators while llama.cpp's Turing fattn-mma uses half2 VKQ accumulators to keep full rate; (5) FA2's hard __CUDA_ARCH__>=800 gate despite compiled-in SM75 atoms; (6) FlashInfer: maintainer statement 'We have a subset of kernels that are compatible with SM75, the only issue is test coverage (we don't have a SM75 [device])' (issue #1648, closed as not planned), and prefill is outright broken on T4 today - BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache fails at first launch even at d=128 because its smem estimate omits SharedStorageQKVO overhead and lands 'just over 64 KB' (issue #3620, opened 2026-06-12, fix PR #3621 open).
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: ROUTE A/B: the bridge program owns the path - no silent fallback, unsupported dims simply stay un-instantiated (v1 contract: s multiple of 64, D in {64,128}; a d=256 instantiation would add a third explicit template case). ROUTE C for FA2: below sm80 the kernel body does not fall back - it prints FATAL and returns garbage/nothing; bf16 silently becomes fp16 (Element forced to half_t in kernel_traits). ROUTE C for FlashInfer: decode dispatches head_dim in {64,128,256} (vLLM's FlashInfer backend validates supported_head_sizes = [64, 128, 256]) but head_dim not a multiple of 64 fails to dispatch and non-multiples of 16 can silently return wrong results (issue #455); the FA2-style prefill path accepts unvalidated head dims at Python level up to memory faults (issue #4299). vLLM as a whole lists compute capability 7.5 as its floor and names T4 as supported; community guidance is that vLLM 0.2.x + CUDA 11.8 with the XFormers backend is the known-good T4 configuration.
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: FlashInfer: no SM75 CI - the maintainer says the blocker is exactly test coverage ('we don't have a SM75' device, issue #1648), and the T4 prefill smem bug (#3620) sat undetected until a user hit it in June 2026 - direct evidence that 'compatible' claims rot without Turing CI. FA2: CI is Ampere+; Turing status is a README pointer ('Support for Turing GPUs (T4, RTX 2080) is coming soon, please use FlashAttention 1.x for Turing GPUs for now', now pointing to ssiu/flash-attention-turing as 'a core subset of FlashAttention features on Turing'); V100 appears in llama.cpp's ggml-ci, and Volta FA logic needed a fix PR (#11615). llama.cpp: fattn-mma configs for Turing/Volta exist in-tree but published perf numbers are RTX 3090/4090, no T4/2080Ti tracking. ssiu/flash-attention-turing: author-validated on T4 only. Bridge kernel: validated locally on Turing hardware (layoutsolve differential fragment conventions, engine correctness gate that caught the h2exp2 fp32-subtract bug on 2026-09-05, per source comments) - the only item in this comparison with first-party Turing CI-style gating.

performance.turing_baseline: Same-hardware (T4/2080Ti-class) numbers found: (1) ssiu/flash-attention-turing (T4, d=64/128, fwd+bwd, mma16x8x8 + ldmatrix): forward up to 2.19x faster than PyTorch SDPA non-causal and 1.95x causal, up to 66% compute throughput (63% in the original issue #1533, 2025-03-12: 'around 2x faster... tested for T4'); backward up to 1.35x/1.51x, 49%/45% throughput. On Turing, SDPA dispatches to xformers Memory-Efficient Attention, so these ratios ARE the same-hardware xformers cutlass FMHA baseline - implying mem-eff fwd runs around 66/2.19 ~= 30% of T4 peak [uncertain: derived, not directly published]. No absolute T4 TFLOPS published by xformers; the cutlass operator is the 'supports more usecases/devices' backend (xformers #950) historically built for Sm60/70/75/80, though recent wheels increasingly ship sm80+ only (build from source with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.5). (2) llama.cpp fattn-mma: PR #11583 'CUDA: use mma PTX instructions for FlashAttention' (merged 2025-02-02) reports pp16384 speedups of 1.1-1.5x vs the previous WMMA path on RTX 3090/4090 (e.g. gemma-2B bs16384: 9059->11881 t/s on 3090; 4090 max 1.50x); NO published T4/2080Ti fattn-mma numbers exist [uncertain], but the in-tree Turing config table (256/256 with nbatch_fa=64, Q_in_reg=true, nstages_target=2 that degrades to synchronous on Turing, half2 VKQ accumulators) makes it a runnable d=256 decode baseline to measure. (3) vLLM PagedAttention V0: runs on T4 (vLLM floor is cc 7.5; known-good vLLM 0.2.x + XFormers backend on T4 per vLLM Discuss) but V0 is a CUDA-core (non-tensor-core) fp16 kernel with no GQA; no official T4 throughput published (PagedAttention paper numbers are A100) [uncertain: community estimates ~15-25 decode t/s single-stream on 7B-class are not primary sources]. (4) FlashInfer on T4: decode subset claimed compatible by maintainer; prefill broken at first launch even at d=128 (#3620); no T4 perf numbers published.
performance.d256_feasibility: ROUTE A (native d=256, 32-row KV tiles): feasible but register-bound. O accumulator acc[D/8][4] = 128 fp32 regs/lane at d=256; S tile shrinks to st[4][4]=16 regs with 32-row KV tiles; keeping Q in registers (qf[32][2] = 64 regs) totals ~208 before temporaries/staging - at or past the 255-reg cliff, hence the Q-in-registers redesign: hold Q in smem, reload A-fragments per k-octave (~16 transient regs), landing near 128+16+overhead ~= 180-200 regs, 1 CTA/SM given 64KB smem. smem must be engineered to exactly 65,536B (zero padding + swizzle) or 50.7KB (32-row Q). ROUTE B (k-chunked 256 on the 128 pipeline): the 128-reg O accumulator is unavoidable (the OUTPUT is 256 wide in both routes), but everything else shrinks: qf 16 regs (reloaded per k-half), K/V smem stays the current 51KB d=128 layout with serial per-half staging, S stays st[8][4]=32 regs on 64-row KV tiles. Numerically identical mma count to ROUTE A; costs 2 extra staging passes + 2 extra __syncthreads per tile and 2x ldmatrix issue. Precedent says the approach is fast: FFPA (issue #1483, DefTruth/ffpa-attn-mma, moved to xlite-dev/ffpa-attn-mma) does exactly this 'GEMM-style' k-chunking at Br x 16 granularity with O(1) SRAM and reaches 105 TFLOPS = 88% of peak on L20 at D=512 (fp32 accum), 1.6-1.9x vs SDPA-EA across L20/A30/4090/3080-mobile at D=320-1024; llama.cpp runs 512/512 and 576/512 (MLA) through the same chunked pattern on Turing-class code paths. ROUTE C (unmodified FA2/FlashInfer): d=256 prefill is structurally blocked on Turing - FA2's shipped d=256 configs need 96-128KB and the only 64KB-fitting traits (64,32,4) exist only as a commented-out line, would run 1 CTA/SM with the synchronous (no-cp.async) gmem path, and the kernel entry refuses to execute below sm80 without a patch; FlashInfer prefill fails at launch even at d=128 on T4 (#3620). FlashInfer DECODE at d=256 on sm_75 is plausible (decode templates cover 64/128/256; decode tiles are small enough for 64KB) but untested/unverified [uncertain].
performance.cost_analysis: ROUTE A: highest effort - new 32-row-KV tile schedule, Q-residency redesign (smem-reloaded A-fragments), exact-64KB smem layout with swizzle (no +8 pad), new causal-mask boundary code for 32-row tiles; risk of spills if Q is kept in regs (~208+ live regs). Payoff: single staging pass per tile (best memory behavior), and it is the config the bridge program fully controls. ROUTE B: lowest effort above d=128 status quo - wrap the existing S and PV sequences in a 2-iteration k-half loop with accumulation; ~2 extra stage+sync per tile (4 vs 2 barrier-class events per tile at 64-row tiles, or keep 32-row tiles at parity); code reuses ldmatrix/mma/softmax primitives untouched; est. 1-2 weeks including a d=256 correctness gate vs torch reference. Expected throughput: same mma count as ROUTE A; FFPA-style chunking loses little to monolithic tiling at fp32-accum (88% SOL at D=512 on L20 is the strongest published datapoint); on Turing the f32-accum half-rate on GeForce caps both routes at ~54 TFLOPS-class peak on 2080 Ti (65 on T4) [uncertain: exact realized fraction]. ROUTE C: engineering cost is deceptive - for FA2 it is 'one gate patch + debugging a 5,000-line kernel never compiled for sm75' (precedents: KLM-corporation/flash-attention-2080ti fork exists; ssiu chose to write a from-scratch Turing port instead, telling evidence; FA2 issues #1342/#1608 document stalled attempts), plus a d=256 dispatch patch to the 64KB (64,32,4) traits; for FlashInfer it means carrying #3621-style fixes and accepting zero-overlap synchronous loads; performance expectation is the ssiu regime (sub-66% SOL with synchronous staging) or worse, i.e. a baseline, not a winner. Compile-time cost of ROUTE C is also real: FA2 instantiates ~100+ template kernels per arch.

design_fit.route: All three routes compared: A = native d=256 bridge template (32-row KV tiles + Q-out-of-registers redesign, 128 fp32 accumulator regs/lane, exact-64KB smem cap); B = k-chunked d=256 on the existing 128 pipeline (two chained 128-deep mma sequences with fp32 accumulation for S=QK^T and PV, serial per-k-half K/V staging to keep smem at 51KB; precedent FA2 #1474/#1483 FFPA and llama.cpp fattn-mma Turing chunked configs); C = bridge-header completeness so unmodified FA2 (SM75_16x8x8 fallback atoms exist in master but kernel bodies are arch-gated at >=800) or FlashInfer (decode-only subset, prefill broken on T4 per #3620) runs on sm_75.
design_fit.recommendation: Do ROUTE B first, ROUTE A second, ROUTE C for baselines only. Rationale: (1) ROUTE B's accumulator problem is identical to ROUTE A's (128 fp32 O regs at d=256 regardless of chunking) and forces the same Q-out-of-registers change, so B's work is a strict subset of A's; (2) the k-chunked approach is performance-proven at exactly this shape class - FFPA reports 88% of peak (105/119 TFLOPS) on L20 at D=512 with fp32 accumulation, 1.6-1.9x vs SDPA-EA, and llama.cpp ships k-chunked 256/256...576/512 configs for Turing in-tree - while no monolithic d=256 kernel exists for 64KB smem anywhere; (3) ROUTE C cannot deliver d=256 prefill on sm_75 at any effort level we control (FA2 needs 96-128KB smem configs and is arch-gated; FlashInfer prefill is broken at d=128 on T4 today, #3620) but DOES deliver the missing same-hardware baselines: run FlashInfer d=256 decode and a patched-FA2 or ssiu-style d=128 fwd on T4/2080Ti to put numbers next to the bridge kernel, and treat llama.cpp fattn-mma 256/256 (build with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.5, fp16 VKQ accumulators, synchronous loads) as the decode baseline to beat. Concrete next actions: (a) implement ROUTE B d=256 in flash_fwd_sm75.cuh behind template<int D> with a 2-step k-half loop, Q in smem re-read per octave, keep h2exp2 path; (b) add a logit-softcap option in the same change (Gemma-2/3 need it at d=256); (c) benchmark bridge-B vs fattn-mma-256 decode and vs ssiu 2.19x/66% SOL at d=128 on T4; (d) decide on ROUTE A only if profiling shows the extra 2 staging+barriers per tile cost >10% of prefill throughput; (e) close ROUTE C as 'baseline harness', not a kernel replacement.
design_fit.numerics_risks: d=256 accumulation order: chunking (ROUTE B) changes fp32 dot-product association vs monolithic (ROUTE A) - last-ulp differences only, both far inside fp16-input tolerance; the real hazard is accumulator PRECISION, not order: llama.cpp's Turing fattn-mma keeps VKQ accumulators in half2 (full-rate mma on GeForce) with FATTN_KQ_MAX_OFFSET and a SOFTMAX_FTZ_THRESHOLD flush, accepting fp16 quantization over 256 k-terms; FFPA explicitly offers F16-accumulation variants as 'faster but riskier' (up to 2.44x vs 1.9x on 4090). The bridge kernel's fp32 PV accumulation is the safe choice but pays the GeForce fp32-accum half mma rate (2080 Ti 54.2 vs 108 TFLOPS; T4 unaffected at 65 both ways per the Turing whitepaper). h2exp2 path: P is produced by ex2.approx.f16x2 on fp16 inputs - the mandatory invariant (already encoded in flash_fwd_sm75.cuh after the 2026-09-05 engine-gate catch) is that (S - m) must be subtracted in fp32 BEFORE packing to half, because raw d=256 dot products exceed fp16 range and pack-first yields inf-inf = NaN; at d=256 the |S| range only grows, so this stays a hard red line, and (S-m) <= 0 flushes safely to 0 in half. Softcap: bridge has none, FA2/FlashInfer/llama.cpp all support logit softcap - Gemma-2/3 (the headline d=256 models) apply tanh softcap ~50, so omitting it blocks the main d=256 workload. bf16: impossible on sm_75 (no hardware bf16; FA2 kernel_traits forces half_t below sm80) - bridge is fp16-only by construction, consistent. FA2/FlashInfer-on-sm75 route adds silent-wrong-output risk: FlashInfer decode head dims that are non-multiples of 16 'silently return wrong results' (#455) and FA2 prefill never validates head_dim (#4299) - any ROUTE C baseline must be differential-tested against torch at the shapes used.
design_fit.demand_weighting: Installed base: T4 remains the cheapest widely-available inference GPU (AWS g4dn-class, cloud spot fleets) and RTX 20xx the large consumer installed base; FlashInfer issue #1648's opening argument is literally 'Tesla T4 and the RTX 20xx series are still the most common GPUs in the market', and vLLM still lists compute capability 7.5 as its official floor with T4 named as supported. Model distribution over head shapes: d=256 demand concentrates in Gemma-2 (2B/9B/27B) and Gemma-3 (d=256, 5:1 sliding:global) - the only mainstream d=256 family likely to be served on Turing-class hardware - plus DeepSeek-style MLA (qk 576 / v 512) for prefill fusion, which is exactly the shape FFPA (#1483) and llama.cpp's 576/512 Turing configs target; d<=128 models vastly outnumber d=256, so the d=256 work is about covering a fast-growing model family (Gemma) and MLA, not the median workload. Beneficiaries: a bridge-native ROUTE A/B keeps the performance crown (and the baseline harness) inside the program while serving Gemma-3-class models on T4/2080Ti; ROUTE C's value is almost entirely strategic - free, credible same-hardware baselines (FlashInfer decode, ssiu/xformers 2.19x-66% SOL at d=128, llama.cpp fattn-mma) to justify the native kernel's existence, since as a replacement it surrenders the load-overlap advantage that is the bridge program's whole reason to exist. [uncertain: exact Gemma-on-Turing serving share]
